topics.name: Inversion after never, seldom, rarely, not only, hardly, no sooner

options: What a heavy bag this is!
How a heavy bag this is!
questions.rule: With a singular noun, use What a + adjective + noun: What a heavy bag!

options: I wish I have more time to rest.
I wish I had more time to rest.
I wish I having more time to rest.
questions.rule: A wish about the present uses the past form: I wish I had.

options: Rarely the twins watch TV on school nights.
Rarely do the twins watches TV on school nights.
Rarely do the twins watch TV on school nights.
questions.rule: After Rarely at the start, invert: do the twins watch (helper + subject + base verb).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Let's rest for a while, shall we?
Let's rest for a while, will we?
Let's rest for a while, don't we?
questions.rule: A suggestion with Let's always takes the tag shall we?

options: Instead of thank the giver, he admired the gifts.
Instead to thank the giver, he admired the gifts.
Instead of thanking the giver, he admired the gifts.
questions.rule: A preposition like instead of is followed by the -ing form: instead of thanking.

options: How weary does the traveller look!
questions.rule: Exclamations keep normal word order: How + adjective + subject + verb. Singular subject: looks.

options: If I were a bird, I would fly over the hills.
If I were a bird, I will fly over the hills.
If I am a bird, I would fly over the hills.
questions.rule: An imaginary situation: If I were ..., I would ...

options: Not only Meera did win the race, but she also broke the school record.
Not only did Meera win the race, but she also broke the school record.
Not only did Meera won the race, but she also broke the school record.
questions.rule: Not only at the start needs inversion: did Meera win (did + subject + base verb).

questions.rule: Imagining being someone else: If I were ..., I would ...

without + -ing form: without saying goodbye.

No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than + simple past.

chat: I got full marks in the maths test!
options: What a great news! Well done!
questions.rule: How + adjective! is correct. News is uncountable, so no 'a'.
Let's + base verb (go), and the tag is shall we?

chat: Why are you looking so sad?
options: I wish I could go on the school trip.
I wish I am going on the school trip.
I wish I was go on the school trip.
questions.rule: A wish about now uses a past form: I wish I could go.

chat: I lost Dad's umbrella. What should I do?
options: If I were you, I would told him the truth.
If I am you, I would tell him the truth.
If I were you, I would tell him the truth.
questions.rule: Advice: If I were you, I would + base verb (tell).

chat: Has Varun ever missed a practice session?
options: No. Not once he has missed a session.
No. Not once has he missed a session.
No. Not once has he miss a session.
questions.rule: Not once at the start needs inversion: has he missed.

chat: What did you do on Sunday?
options: Instead of going out, I stayed home and read a book.
Instead of go out, I stayed home and read a book.
Instead of going out, I stays home and read a book.
questions.rule: instead of + -ing (going), and the past tense stayed for Sunday.

chat: We have finished the project at last!
options: Great! Let's celebrated with ice cream, shall we?
Great! Let's celebrate with ice cream, won't we?
Great! Let's celebrate with ice cream, shall we?
questions.rule: Let's + base verb (celebrate) and the tag shall we?

chat: The concert was amazing. Where were you?
options: I know. I wish I had came with you.
I know. I wish I have come with you.
I know. I wish I had come with you.
questions.rule: Regret about the past: wish + had + past participle (had come).

questions.source: What a lovely garden it is!
options: It is a very lovely garden.
It a very lovely garden is.
questions.rule: What a becomes a very: It is a very lovely garden.

questions.source: How weary the old farmer looks!
options: The old farmer looks very weary.
The old farmer look very weary.
The old farmer looks very wearily.
questions.rule: How + adjective becomes very + adjective; after 'looks' keep the adjective.

questions.source: It is a very precious jewel.
options: What a precious jewel it is!
How a precious jewel it is!
questions.rule: a very + adjective + noun becomes What a + adjective + noun ... !

questions.source: I have never seen such a crowded station.
options: Never I have seen such a crowded station.
Never have I seen such a crowded station.
Never have I saw such a crowded station.
questions.rule: Starting with Never, put the helper before the subject: have I seen.

questions.source: I am sorry I did not get up sooner.
options: I wish I had got up sooner.
I wish I have got up sooner.
I wish I had get up sooner.
questions.rule: Regret about the past: I wish I had got up sooner.

questions.source: Neha sings well and she also dances well.
options: Not only does Neha sings well, but she also dances well.
Not only does Neha sing well, but she also dances well.
Not only did Neha sing well, but she also dances well.
questions.rule: Present tense: Not only does + subject + base verb (sing).

questions.source: I am not a bird, so I cannot fly to the mountains.
options: If I were a bird, I can fly to the mountains.
If I were a bird, I could flew to the mountains.
If I were a bird, I could fly to the mountains.
questions.rule: Unreal present: If I were ..., I could + base verb (fly).

questions.source: As soon as the teacher entered, the class became silent.
options: Hardly the teacher had entered when the class became silent.
Hardly had the teacher entered than the class became silent.
Hardly had the teacher entered when the class became silent.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle ... when (not 'than').
